detail.text: Inspect the handling unit for damage before it is moved into the warehouse, as damage found later cannot be claimed against the carrier.
Determine whether the damage is to the outer packaging only or includes the product itself, as this determines whether to refuse the delivery or accept and block it.

If the damage is to the outer packaging only and product is intact: take photos of the damaged packaging, post the goods receipt to blocked stock, notify the QA inspector, and note the damage on the delivery note.
If the product itself is visibly damaged: post the affected quantity to blocked stock, label the handling unit 'BLOCKED - QA', and notify the QA inspector.

detail.text: Do not mix damaged and undamaged units on one pallet.
Photos must show the handling unit label and the damage, and must be attached to the goods receipt in the WMS.

Confirm whether the damage is visible on the outer packaging only, or whether the product inside is also damaged, as this determines whether to refuse the delivery (outer packaging only) or accept and block it (product intact).
Confirm whether the seal is broken or the packaging is wet, as this would require moving the unit to quarantine area Q-01 instead of the standard handling procedure.
Notify the QA inspector when product damage is found or when outer packaging is damaged but product is intact.
Refuse the delivery and note the reason on the delivery note before the driver leaves if the outer packaging shows visible damage and the product is not confirmed intact.
